scope.statement: This engagement is delivered over [TBD: number] weeks in [TBD: one track / two parallel tracks]: Track A migrates mail and files, and Track B moves sign-in and devices to Google Workspace.
out_of_scope_extra: Migration of Microsoft Teams chat history and channel conversations. Files stored in Teams channels are migrated with their SharePoint sites where listed in the site mapping.
Migration of Planner, Power Automate, Power Apps and Forms content.
Conversion of OneNote notebooks. Notebook files are moved as files and are not converted.
Migration of public folders and of PST files stored on PCs or file shares, unless listed in the user mapping.
Clean-up of SharePoint permissions or content before migration.
Retirement of the Microsoft 365 tenant, Exchange servers or the old directory. A retirement plan is delivered; the work is performed by [TBD: Customer].
End-user training beyond [TBD: number] sessions, and support beyond [TBD: number] weeks after cutover.

assumptions: [TBD: Customer] provides a dedicated administrator account on Microsoft 365 and a dedicated super administrator account on Google Workspace before work starts. Both are removed at closeout.
[TBD: Customer] makes DNS changes within the agreed change window, or grants Premier Cloud access to do so.
Microsoft 365 licences remain active until the final delta pass is complete and validated.
success_criteria: Every in-scope mailbox, OneDrive account and mapped SharePoint site is migrated, shown by the migration tool's reconciliation report for each batch.
Mail flows to and from Google Workspace for every in-scope domain after cutover, verified by test messages in both directions.
Every in-scope user can sign in to Google Workspace using the agreed sign-in method.
Calendar resources and Google Groups exist for every in-scope room and equipment mailbox and distribution list.
Each application listed under Identity signs in through the agreed identity provider, verified against its test plan.
The cutover runbook and the post-migration validation report are delivered.

appendices.title: Migration Watchpoints
appendices.body:
The following are known limits of moving from Microsoft 365 to Google Workspace. Keep the ones that apply to this migration and say what each means for [TBD: Customer].

- **Large accounts.** Google limits how much data one user can receive per day. Mailboxes and OneDrive accounts above that limit take more than one day to move and are scheduled in their own sync window.
- **Large SharePoint libraries.** A shared drive holds a limited number of items. Libraries above that limit are split across more than one shared drive in the site mapping.
- **Permissions.** SharePoint permissions that break inheritance at folder or file level do not map one to one onto shared drive roles. Affected content is listed in discovery and its access agreed before migration.
- **Content that does not convert.** Teams chats, OneNote notebooks, Planner plans and some mailbox settings are not converted. Each is either out of scope or listed in the cutover runbook with what users should expect.
- **Systems that send mail.** Scanners, printers and applications that send mail through Microsoft 365 stop working at MX cutover unless they are reconfigured. Each is listed in discovery with an owner.
- **Sign-in changes.** Applications that sign in through Microsoft need re-pointing before the old directory is retired. Users may need to sign in again to third-party tools after cutover.
- **Licences.** Microsoft 365 licences must stay active until the final delta pass is validated.
